question: Explain how a potentiometer can measure the emf of a cell more accurately than a voltmeter, considering internal resistance.

options.A: A potentiometer uses a null method: at balance it draws no current from the cell, so there is no internal drop $Ir$ and it measures the emf. A voltmeter draws some current and generally measures the terminal potential difference
options.B: A potentiometer is more accurate because it has a lower resistance and therefore draws a larger current from the cell
options.C: A voltmeter always measures the emf exactly because its reading is independent of the current through the cell
options.D: A potentiometer measures terminal potential difference only because current must flow through the test cell at balance
